title: Integral triangular PBW basis for the divided-power enveloping ring
statement: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional split semisimple rational Lie algebra [def-wf-lie-algebra], [def-wf-semisimple-lie-algebra], with splitting maximal abelian subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, root system $R$, positive roots $R^+$ and simple roots $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r$. Fix a Chevalley basis $h_i,e_\alpha$: $h_i$ are the simple coroots forming a basis of $\mathfrak h$, $e_\alpha$ span the root spaces, $[h,e_\alpha]=\alpha(h)e_\alpha$, $[e_\alpha,e_{-\alpha}]=h_\alpha$, and $[e_\alpha,e_\beta]=\pm(p_{\alpha,\beta}+1)e_{\alpha+\beta}$ when $\alpha+\beta$ is a root, with zero bracket when the sum is neither a root nor zero; $p_{\alpha,\beta}$ is the largest $p\ge0$ for which $\beta-p\alpha$ is a root. Let $U_{\mathbf Q}$ be the associative algebra with unit generated by $\mathfrak g$ subject to $xy-yx=[x,y]$, and let $U_{\mathbf Z}$ be its unital $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra generated by every $e_\alpha^{(m)}=e_\alpha^m/m!$ ($\alpha\in R$, $m\ge0$). Choose any ordering $\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_N$ of $R^+$. The ordered elements $$\left(\prod_{j=1}^N e_{-\beta_j}^{(a_j)}\right)\left(\prod_{i=1}^r\binom{h_i}{b_i}\right)\left(\prod_{j=1}^N e_{\beta_j}^{(c_j)}\right),\qquad a_j,b_i,c_j\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0},$$ form a $\mathbf Z$-basis of $U_{\mathbf Z}$. Here $\binom{h}{b}=h(h-1)\cdots(h-b+1)/b!$ and the factor for $b=0$ is $1$. In particular every displayed element belongs to $U_{\mathbf Z}$ and every element of $U_{\mathbf Z}$ is an integer linear combination of them. A representation of $\mathfrak g$ extends uniquely to an action of $U_{\mathbf Q}$; the algebra homomorphism is the one sending each generator $x$ to its representing operator. The zero Lie algebra gives $U_{\mathbf Z}=\mathbf Z$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-root-base-rational-integral-spans] to the root/coroot pairing on $\mathfrak h^\vee\times\mathfrak h$. Thus $h_\alpha=\sum_i u_i h_i$ with $u_i\in\mathbf Z$ for every root, and the root pairings $\alpha(h_i)$ are integers. By [lem-sfb-integral-newton-expansion], every $\binom{s+\sum_i u_ih_i}{t}$ is an integer combination of $\prod_i\binom{h_i}{b_i}$ with $\sum b_i\le t$. Products of toral binomials also have integral expansions, of degree no larger than the sum of their degrees: their defining polynomials take integer values on all integer tuples. Here and below the $h_i$ commute, so these polynomial identities may be evaluated in $U_{\mathbf Q}$.

source.place: Section 23h, pp.509--510, supporting integral-enveloping-algebra argument (agent reconstruction; full Kostant/Steinberg proof source unavailable)

proof.text: First prove $\binom{h_i}{b}\in U_{\mathbf Z}$ by induction on $b$, for each simple root. The case $b=0$ is $1$. For $b>0$, put $E=e_{\alpha_i}$, $F=e_{-\alpha_i}$, $H=h_i$. The defining Chevalley relations give the three hypotheses of [lem-sfb-sl2-divided-straightening]. Its identity with $m=n=b$ has $t=b$ term $\binom{h_i}{b}$ and all other terms $F^{(b-t)}\binom{h_i-2b+2t}{t}E^{(b-t)}$ with $t<b$. By [lem-sfb-integral-newton-expansion] each middle factor is an integer combination of $\binom{h_i}{j}$ for $j\le t$. These are in $U_{\mathbf Z}$ by induction; all root divided powers are generators. Subtract the $t<b$ terms from $E^{(b)}F^{(b)}$ to obtain the claim. Thus every displayed triangular element is in $U_{\mathbf Z}$.

source.place: Section 23h, pp.509--510, supporting integral-enveloping-algebra argument (agent reconstruction; full Kostant/Steinberg proof source unavailable)

proof.text: Use blocks $e_\alpha^{(a)}$ and $\binom{h_i}{b}$, omitting degree-zero blocks, and give them degrees $a$ and $b$. For distinct nonopposite roots, [lem-sfb-chevalley-rank-two-straightening] swaps two root blocks with integer lower-total-degree corrections. For opposite roots, apply [lem-sfb-sl2-divided-straightening] with $(E,F,H)=(e_\alpha,e_{-\alpha},h_\alpha)$: the $t=0$ term is the swap; a $t>0$ term has degree at most $(m-t)+(n-t)+t=m+n-t$ after expanding its Cartan factor by Step 1, hence has strictly smaller degree. These rules apply in either direction by replacing $\alpha$ with $-\alpha$. For a toral/root swap use $P(h_i)e_\alpha^{(a)}=e_\alpha^{(a)}P(h_i+a\alpha(h_i))$, obtained by repeatedly using $h_ie_\alpha-e_\alpha h_i=\alpha(h_i)e_\alpha$. For $P(X)=\binom{X}{b}$, the shift minus $P(X)$ has degree less than $b$, takes integer values, and so has an integral lower-degree binomial expansion by [lem-sfb-integral-newton-expansion].

source.place: Section 23h, pp.509--510, supporting integral-enveloping-algebra argument (agent reconstruction; full Kostant/Steinberg proof source unavailable)

proof.text: Let $M$ be the integer span of the proposed triangular elements. Every word in the blocks lies in $M$, by induction first on total degree $D$, and then on inversions in its expanded sequence of block types. The type order is $e_{-\beta_1},\ldots,e_{-\beta_N},h_1,\ldots,h_r,e_{\beta_1},\ldots,e_{\beta_N}$; a degree-$a$ block contributes $a$ copies of its type. At degree zero the word is $1$. Swap any adjacent distinct inverted block types using Step 3. The leading swap decreases inversions, and all correction words have degree less than $D$, so the two induction hypotheses apply. Cartan blocks of distinct types commute. When all types are sorted, adjacent equal root blocks merge using $X^{(a)}X^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}X^{(a+b)}$; equal toral blocks merge by the integral polynomial expansion of Step 1. Their expansion terms still have sorted types, and degree at most $D$. Repeating the merge for each type gives precisely integer combinations of triangular elements. This proves the induction, including arbitrary orders of the positive roots; it does not presume that $M$ is a ring.

source.place: Section 23h, pp.509--510, supporting integral-enveloping-algebra argument (agent reconstruction; full Kostant/Steinberg proof source unavailable)

proof.text: Each element of $U_{\mathbf Z}$ is a finite integer combination of words in root divided powers, by the definition of the generated unital $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra. Step 4 puts all these words in $M$. Conversely Step 2 puts every generator of the integer span $M$ in $U_{\mathbf Z}$. Hence $M=U_{\mathbf Z}$, proving the spanning and membership assertions.

source.place: Section 23h, pp.509--510, supporting integral-enveloping-algebra argument (agent reconstruction; full Kostant/Steinberg proof source unavailable)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-rational-pbw] to the ordered rational basis $e_{-\beta_1},\ldots,e_{-\beta_N},h_1,\ldots,h_r,e_{\beta_1},\ldots,e_{\beta_N}$. In its ordinary PBW expansion, the triangular element of index $(a,b,c)$ has leading term the matching ordered monomial times the nonzero rational coefficient $1/(\prod a_j!\prod b_i!\prod c_j!)$; all other terms have smaller total degree, because each $\binom{h_i}{b_i}$ has top term $h_i^{b_i}/b_i!$. In any finite rational relation, take the largest total degree. Distinct indices give distinct PBW monomials in that degree, so all coefficients in that degree vanish. Descending on degree proves rational linear independence and therefore integer linear independence. Together with Step 5 this is the claimed integer basis.

source.place: Section 23h, pp.509--510, supporting integral-enveloping-algebra argument (agent reconstruction; full Kostant/Steinberg proof source unavailable)

proof.text: For a representation $\rho:\mathfrak g\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbf Q}(V)$, the defining Lie-representation identity is exactly the hypothesis on $f$ in [lem-sfb-enveloping-universal-property]. Take $A=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbf Q}(V)$ to obtain the unique algebra action, with the required generator values. If $\mathfrak g=0$, [lem-sfb-rational-pbw] identifies $U_{\mathbf Q}$ with $\mathbf Q$ and its sole PBW monomial with $1$. There are no root generators, so the unital integer subalgebra is exactly the integer multiples of $1$, namely $\mathbf Z$.
